Export a measurement model to Stan or brms

Source: R/api-model-export.R
export_mfrm_model.Rd

Write a self-contained Bayesian model bundle without running an estimator. Supports ordinary RSM/PCM and fixed-population one-family GPCM MML fits in both formats. Estimated-population one-family GPCM and two-family GPCM use Stan. Fixed facet/group and step anchors are retained. Sources must be unit-weight, with a fixed standard-normal Person population or (Stan only, one-family GPCM) an estimated intercept-only normal population, and no facet interactions or post-fit shrinkage. Unsupported specifications fail before files are written.

Usage

export_mfrm_model(
  fit,
  output_dir,
  format = c("stan", "brms"),
  location_prior_sd = 1,
  step_prior_sd = 1,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  acknowledge_sensitive = FALSE,
  log_slope_prior_sd = 1,
  population_prior = list(mean = c(0, 1), log_sd = c(0, 0.5))
)

Arguments

fit

A native RSM/PCM or GPCM MML mfrm_fit returned by fit_mfrm().

output_dir

Destination directory. The bundle includes observed ratings and original level labels; review it before sharing.

format

Either "stan" (CmdStanR) or "brms" (custom family).

location_prior_sd

Positive marginal prior SD for each varying facet location; fixed or uniquely determined locations have zero prior SD.

step_prior_sd

Positive marginal prior SD for each varying step offset.

overwrite

Replace bundle files that already exist? Defaults to FALSE.

acknowledge_sensitive

Suppress the reminder that ratings and original identifiers are included. Defaults to FALSE.

log_slope_prior_sd

Positive marginal prior SD of each component log slope for GPCM export. Defaults to 1; inspect prior sensitivity. Not used by RSM/PCM models.

population_prior

Normal prior parameters for an estimated Person population: a named list with mean = c(location, scale) for its mean and log_sd = c(location, scale) for the log of its standard deviation. Each scale must be positive. Defaults give mu ~ normal(0, 1) and log(sigma) ~ normal(0, 0.5). Unused for fixed-population exports.

Value

Invisibly, a list with format, model, output_dir and named files. No model is fitted and no software is installed.

Details

The default one-family GPCM estimates its population mean and variance. Its intercept-only population can be exported to Stan, retaining the native metric, relative-slope constraint and supported fixed anchors. The generated model uses theta = mu + sigma * z, with independent standard-normal z. The population mean and SD are sampled, not fixed at their MML estimates. population_prior adds explicit Bayesian priors: by default sigma has median 1 and a central 95% prior interval of approximately 0.38 to 2.66. These are starting assumptions, not a population-size recommendation; inspect prior predictions and sensitivity for your rubric and anchors. The displayed Person prior SD includes uncertainty in both mu and sigma, not only sigma. Population regression, estimated-mean models with a fixed SD, and estimated-population brms or two-family exports are not supported. Choosing gpcm_mml_identification = "fixed_standard_normal" changes the model; it is not a file-format conversion or a workaround for these exclusions.

Both formats retain the category ladder, facet signs, facet centering and RSM/PCM step ownership of the source specification. RSM/PCM adjacent-category log odds are theta + signed facet locations - step. Steps follow their declared within-owner sum targets (zero by default) and are not ordered. A binary ladder has its single offset fixed at its target. Fixed-population ability parameters have independent standard-normal priors; realized abilities are not centered across the observed Persons in either population mode.

All supported exports preserve the native logistic metric (L-metric), with scaling constant \(D = 1\). No extra 1.7 or 1.702 factor is used. Standard-normal ability priors do not imply a normal-ogive response link. The "Logistic metric (D = 1)" section of fit_mfrm() explains the scale and the adjustments needed before comparing other parameterizations.

Centered locations and steps use an orthonormal contrast basis. Independent normal coordinates are scaled so each constrained component has the requested marginal SD. A centered singleton is fixed at zero. Uncentered locations have independent normal priors. These proper structural priors are additions to MML: the Bayesian posterior is not a reproduction of MML point estimates or frequentist confidence intervals. Review prior sensitivity for the application.

Two-family GPCM is available with format = "stan" only. Its effective slope is the product of the two component slopes and multiplies the entire adjacent-category predictor, including locations and steps. The first family's log slopes sum to zero; the second family's log slopes are free on the fixed N(0,1) ability scale. Normal priors on orthonormal/free log-slope coordinates give each component the specified marginal log-slope SD. slope-levels.csv maps the generated component_slopes and log_component_slopes to their owners and levels. This preserves the source likelihood, not an MML interval or the exact priors/program of Uto and Ueno (2020). In particular, the extra 1.7 multiplier in their Appendix is absent. One-family GPCM supports both formats. Its single owner's log slopes sum to zero (geometric mean one); its slope also multiplies the entire predictor. A singleton slope owner is fixed at one.

Fixed non-Person facet anchors, group means and step anchors are exact affine constraints. The export preserves whole-facet versus remainder centering and each step owner's target. Priors on the remaining free contrasts are centered so each free level shares its block's remaining total equally. These priors are defined on the constrained subspace, not obtained by conditioning an earlier unanchored posterior. levels.csv and steps.csv in these bundles record the affine prior means, marginal SDs and fixed-coordinate indicators; model-data.rds$constraints retains the source constraints. One-family bundles use the same affine representation even without anchors. Anchors are fixed inputs: zero posterior spread does not establish certainty about their earlier calibration. Uncertain external calibration is not propagated. Retained step constraints are exported; this does not add a step-anchor fitting argument. Native two-family fitting retains its anchor exclusion. Person anchors require JML in native fitting and remain outside this MML exporter.

model-data.rds records the design matrices, priors and mappings used by both formats. levels.csv maps original labels to generated parameters; categories.csv maps Stan/brms categories to the source score scale. run.R fits the exported model and saves draws, diagnostics and replicated ratings. Run it from the bundle directory, after installing CmdStanR/CmdStan and, for the brms format, brms. Neither is required to export a bundle. Both formats support Rscript run.R --summarize to regenerate summaries from fit.rds without compiling or sampling. Keep model-data.rds, summarize.R and the brms model.R with the saved fit. Read summary-decision.csv first, then sampling-review.csv for the checks, criteria and next actions. parameter-summary.csv joins original labels to estimates, references and score-direction notes. value_role distinguishes estimated values, fixed anchors and constraint-determined values. Fixed values have no estimated SD or interval (NA); they do not establish zero external calibration uncertainty. Varying parameters retain equal-tailed 95% credible bounds, endpoint MCSE, R-hat and bulk/tail ESS, even during review, with interval_status beside the values. interval_computed means finite bounds for a varying parameter, not reliable sampling or coverage. sampler-diagnostics.csv contains per-chain diagnostics; posterior-summary.rds retains all four tables and interpretation notes.

The screen checks at least four chains, R-hat below 1.01, bulk/tail ESS at least 100 per chain, zero divergences/tree-depth hits and E-BFMI at least 0.3. Missing diagnostics require review; fixed coordinates are excluded using model constraints, not sample variance. Tree-depth hits flag efficiency separately from divergences. These checks follow the Stan diagnostic guidance and are not a certificate of validity. Review all varying coordinates, model fit and priors. The larger endpoint MCSE divided by interval width measures simulation precision; no universal acceptable fraction is imposed. Read the matching summary and model-data files with read_mfrm_posterior() to use summary(), plot(), stored credible intervals and mfrm_report() without either sampling backend. Keep fit.rds for joint-draw calculations. Generated brms callbacks support log_lik(), posterior_predict() and posterior_epred(); the last returns category probabilities.

Log likelihood and replicated ratings condition on the sampled abilities of existing Persons. They do not provide leave-one-Person-out validation or predictions for new Persons. Exporting does not qualify the original fit's convergence, inference, or an external sampler's diagnostics. Repeated ratings retain the source conditional-independence assumption.

References

Uto, M., & Ueno, M. (2020). A generalized many-facet Rasch model and its Bayesian estimation using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo. Behaviormetrika, 47, 469-496. doi:10.1007/s41237-020-00115-7 . Equation 9, Sections 6-7 and Appendix.

See also

export_mfrm_results(), fit_mfrm()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("export_mfrm_model", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
# Illustrative fixed reference; applications need justified calibration values.
anchor <- data.frame(Facet = "Rater",
                     Level = as.character(ratings$Rater[1]), Anchor = 0)
fit <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                 model = "GPCM", method = "MML", step_facet = "Criterion",
                 slope_facet = "Criterion", anchors = anchor,
                 anchor_policy = "silent")
# Keep the default estimated population. The example data are synthetic.
# Export needs neither Stan nor brms installed and runs no sampler.
stan <- export_mfrm_model(fit, tempfile("mfrmr-stan-"), "stan",
                           acknowledge_sensitive = TRUE)
names(stan$files)
bundle <- readRDS(stan$files[["model-data.rds"]])
bundle$categories # Generated categories mapped to original scores
bundle$population # Estimated mean/SD and their priors
bundle$priors
# Run this bundle's run.R separately if external sampling is wanted.
unlink(stan$output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
} # }
